 David Corenswet Faces PR Disaster On Mr. Irrelevant Press Tour (Exclusive)
 MM 
 By Matt McGloin 
 November 11, 2026 2:37pm 
 5 min read 
 💬 0 Comments 
 UPDATE: Insiders now say the movie is dead, no reshoots, and Corenswet’s Broadway run leaves no window to fix it .
 David Corenswet has a movie to sell this Christmas. Our Skydance Paramount insider says the sales job now comes with a PR disaster attached.
 Corenswet stars in Mr. Irrelevant , the John Tuggle NFL biopic opening only in theaters December 25 from Paramount.
 A Christmas release means a December press tour. That tour now lands weeks after Skydance fired James Gunn and Peter Safran at DC Studios , and days after our insiders said Corenswet is done as Superman .

 Before we dive in, let's address James Gunn's post on Threads. Worth mentioning is that it's always been the case in the... 
 “David C’s movie coming out late Dec! His people & studio will have to do HEAVY damage control during press tour. Wow good luck!!!” 
 The insider does not see a soft landing coming.
 “Trainwreck incoming for David, the face of failure.”
 That matches what the same sources said Tuesday, calling Corenswet “the face of Gunn’s failure” while confirming his DC contract ends with Man of Tomorrow .
 David Corenswet and Isabela May star in Mr. Irrelevant 
 ‘Gonna Have To Come Up With A Way To Deal With This’
 The junket interviews are supposed to sell an inspirational true-story football movie. 
 Instead, Corenswet will be sitting down to questions about a DC Universe that collapsed between his two Superman movies.
 Since Monday’s firing, Puck News reports Skydance is dismantling Gunn’s DCU slate , and reports and insiders say Man of Tomorrow might not even hit theaters .
 Every one of those questions is coming to the Mr. Irrelevant junket.
 “He and his people are gonna have to come up with a way to deal with this,” says the insider, who already sees the obvious play.
 “Easiest one is to throw Gunn under the bus, blame his ‘quirky’ sensibilities etc.” 
 Gunn wrote the opening for that one himself. His goodbye post called his four years running DC “trying” and pointed at his “ADHD hyperfocus” struggling with the studio-head job. 
 Our insiders already said Gunn posted that to get ahead of the bad-behavior stories they say are coming .
 Skipping the tour is not an option, either. Mr. Irrelevant is David Ellison’s own production, made through Skydance Sports with Dana Goldberg and Don Granger producing, and THR reported it tested through the roof . 
 Paramount handed it Christmas Day. The people selling Corenswet’s football movie are the same people who just fired his DC boss.

 James Gunn and David Corenswet behind-the-scenes Superman 
 Corenswet Already Argued With Gunn On The Superman Set
 If Corenswet’s camp does point at Gunn, the clips already exist.
 Official Superman behind-the-scenes footage released last year showed Gunn and Corenswet in a heated on-set argument over the movie’s climactic speech to Lex Luthor. 
 Gunn wanted a big, emotional take. Corenswet questioned why Superman would yell, saying “I feel weak with me yelling at him,” and walked off the set to think it over before playing the scene.
 Corenswet brought up the dynamic again in Variety’s Actors on Actors conversation with Jonathan Bailey, revealing he and Gunn also disagreed over the final kiss with Lois Lane. 
 Gunn wanted it solemn. Corenswet wanted Clark to chuckle when Lois says she loves him. Corenswet’s version is the one in the movie.
 The Juilliard-trained actor has never hidden that he had his own ideas about how to play Superman. His viral audition tape, which fans argued topped Gunn’s theatrical take , made the same point for him.
 Those stories read as charming collaboration when Superman was riding high. With Gunn fired, they read as a record that the actor and the director did not always agree on the character.
 Milly Alcock Already Showed How This Goes
 There is already a road map for quietly exiting Gunn’s DC. Milly Alcock drew it.
 When Clayface premiered in October, Alcock wiped Supergirl from her Instagram .
 Insiders then told us her Man of Tomorrow role had been reduced down to a cameo, and days later that she was done, with a new manager and her three-movie DC contract fulfilled .
 Her first project since? A London stage play, not DC .
 Corenswet sits in the same contract spot. “David’s contract ends with MOT,” the insider told us Tuesday.
 The difference is Alcock got to go quiet. Corenswet has to spend December in front of cameras selling a movie while every interviewer asks about the cape.
 Nicholas Hoult, David Corenswet and James Gunn behind-the-scenes of Superman 
 ‘Expect More Stories To Come Out’
 These are the sources that have been ahead of the DC story all fall.
 On October 2, they said Corenswet keeps Superman only if Man of Tomorrow makes money . On October 21, they said Corenswet got the same three-movie contract as Alcock .
 On November 9, the day of the firing, they told us Gunn was fired so he would have no say over the final cut and that “people already knew,” pointing at the Alcock deletions and “Corenswet and Hoult auditions.”
 On Tuesday, they said Corenswet is done as Superman, with Skydance bracing for a $100 million loss .
 And after the firing, they said to expect more stories to come out. “Bad stories.” 
 Mr. Irrelevant opens December 25. Jeremy Latcham takes over DC Studios on December 1. The press tour lands in between, and per our insider, that is how long Corenswet’s people have to come up with a way to deal with this.
